**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §2.5. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

When two features carry the same information, parameters may not be identifiable. Linear independence asks whether any feature vector can be produced by combining the others.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
a_1\boldsymbol v_1+\cdots+a_k\boldsymbol v_k=\boldsymbol0\Longrightarrow a_1=\cdots=a_k=0
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

The vectors (1,1) and (2,2) are dependent because 2(1,1)-(2,2)=0. Distance and doubled distance cannot independently identify two regression coefficients: several coefficient pairs produce identical predictions.

## What follows, and what does not

Independence is a property of a set of vectors, not a statement that statistical random variables are independent. Chapter 6 uses 'independence' in a different probabilistic sense.

## Test your reasoning

Are (1,1) and (1,-1) independent? Solve a(1,1)+b(1,-1)=0.
